content:
A battery energy storage system, or BESS, stores electricity for later use. An insurance assessment needs more than its investment amount or battery capacity: modules, converters, control equipment, cooling and site arrangements form an interconnected installation. A solar-panel policy does not automatically establish protection for an added battery system. The photovoltaic equipment assessment should remain distinct from this battery-system review.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. Planning material for 2027; the scenarios below are hypothetical, not incident or demand forecasts.

Who should prepare a BESS risk file?

The discussion is relevant to energy producers, industrial consumers, project investors and businesses adding storage to an existing installation. State who owns the battery equipment, who operates it and which party maintains it. If several companies participate, separate their interests instead of naming only the project.

Record both power and energy capacity as shown in technical documents, without treating them as interchangeable indicators. Identify operating equipment separately from storage, installation, testing and commissioning stages. Each stage raises different insurance questions.

Risk scenarios are not a coverage list

Ask about fire, accidental physical damage, internal breakdown and consequences affecting surrounding property. Describe the system using manufacturer and competent technical records, not an improvised safety assessment. This article gives no instruction for handling batteries or modifying protective systems.

Read the proposal's treatment of gradual capacity loss, expected degradation, known defects, warranty issues, cyber events and losses without physical damage. Ask which emergency, removal, decontamination or replacement expenses could be considered and whether they have separate limits. Their necessity does not establish insurance inclusion.

What is genuinely relevant to 2027?

In its publication of 15 October 2026, checked on 25 November 2026, the Ministry of Energy described proposed import measures in its discussion of 2027 fiscal policy. This dated publication establishes what was proposed then, not its present legislative status. It does not confirm an enacted exemption, eligibility or a guaranteed investment outcome. The practical inference is to review newly planned storage separately, not forecast demand for insurance.

For insurance planning, distinguish fiscal treatment from equipment value and operational risk. If the project adds storage in 2027, obtain a fresh description before assuming an existing solar or property programme accepts it. A finance model and an insurance contract serve different purposes.

Prevention and operational change

Keep competent service checks, warning records and unresolved manufacturer recommendations traceable. Ask how changes to modules, cooling or controls affect the approved technical configuration; do not modify a battery system to satisfy an enquiry. Prevention means following the applicable technical and safety process, not assuming that insurance replaces it.

Price and business interruption

No verified premium for this project's 2027 period is available here. An individual calculation requires the actual configuration, documented values, location, commissioning stage, maintenance and requested protections. The premium is the policy price; the deductible is the insured's contractually retained part of a loss. (BNM: contract terms, checked 25 November 2026; general guidance, not individual policy conditions.)

Use a hypothetical recovery exercise: one component becomes unavailable and compatible replacement must be ordered. Separate equipment repair, access, transport and the business effects of downtime. A fall in trading revenue, a change in electricity prices and physical damage are different events. Do not promise reimbursement for all of them.

Documents before seeking a proposal

Prepare a component inventory, technical and acceptance records, service arrangements, warranty documents, known defects and a dated value basis. Describe relationships with the solar installation or the network where relevant. Sensitive diagrams and operational access should remain in controlled channels, not public enquiry forms.

Three situations: what to compare before deciding

The MOLDASIG property page, rechecked on 26 November 2026, presents machinery breakdown separately from property and interruption. It is not dedicated BESS wording. This review has not verified a storage product or ING placement for the project.

  • Delivered but not commissioned: compare storage, installation, testing and operation. Prepare the programme, manufacturer records and handover documents. Ask which stage can be considered; purchase is neither technical nor insurance acceptance.
  • Capacity declines or a component fails: compare performance history, manufacturer recommendations and competent findings. Separate gradual change from a sudden observed event without diagnosing it in the enquiry. Check definitions, warranty and expenses for the specific component.
  • Storage connects to solar or trading in 2027: compare equipment damage with a separate revenue scenario. Prepare configuration, values and operating assumptions. Check availability and financial-loss triggers instead of treating electricity-price changes as physical damage.

Frequently asked questions

What determines a BESS insurance calculation?

Provide the actual configuration, supported values, location, operating or commissioning stage, maintenance and requested protections. Identify the relationship with solar and surrounding property. Compare like-for-like limits, deductible and expense treatment; battery capacity or project investment alone is not a verified premium or evidence that the whole system has been accepted.

What documents should the project team prepare?

Gather the component inventory, ownership and project-role documents, manufacturer information, technical and acceptance records, warranties, service arrangements and known recommendations. Separate power from energy capacity using the actual records. Share detailed drawings only through controlled channels; an insurance enquiry should not receive system credentials or operational access.

What should we retain after a battery-system warning or incident?

Follow competent safety and emergency instructions rather than an insurance article. Do not approach, open or handle a potentially dangerous battery to collect evidence. Keep safely available warning times, monitoring records and authorized findings. Notify under the actual contract and ask about inspection and restoration; an alert alone does not establish an insured event.

Is normal capacity degradation an insured breakdown?

Do not equate gradual performance change with accidental damage. Compare manufacturer records and the technical cause with the policy definitions, warranty provisions and exclusions. Ask which component and expenses could be considered. A replacement recommendation or reduced trading performance does not itself establish a covered breakdown or compensation amount.

Can the published 2027 fiscal proposal be treated as a benefit already secured?

The Ministry of Energy publication of 15 October 2026 records a proposal at that time, not its final legislative status or your eligibility. Before relying on a benefit, check adopted rules and applicable conditions with a specialist. Fiscal treatment and insurance acceptance remain separate assessments even within the same project.

Contact ING Broker to check assessment possibilities. The broker does not certify battery safety or guarantee specialized cover. Availability, risk acceptance and claims decisions belong to the insurer under its contract.
